summary: Source validation passes the source path as the missing-path label instead of passing `--source`.
Source tokenization appends each normalized whitespace token as one list element even when normalization expands it into multiple words.
Wav2Vec2 character offsets are treated as CTC frame indices when constructing word timestamps and confidences.
The English-only Wav2Vec2 checkpoint is used for every requested language and then reports the requested language as successful detection.
The ASR chunk limit treats zero as unlimited and is not propagated to fallback backends.
The whole-file whisper.cpp transcription has a fixed one-hour subprocess timeout.
A requested diarization pass converts every model or decode failure into an empty successful result.
Resume reconstructs the source cursor from the beginning of the ASR rather than from the checkpoint's source position.
The numbered batch fallback validates that output numbers are in range but ignores their values when ordering annotations.
The full-batch fallback adds the current chunk to context before constructing its supposedly previous-context prompt.
A mixed-speaker audio chunk is assigned one majority speaker even when multiple speakers occur inside it.
The source divergence preflight aborts even when `--keep-unaligned` was explicitly supplied.
Explicit `--diarize` is accepted without requiring an HF token while `--auto-detect-speakers` requires one.
Fresh runs preserve and later consume enriched and diarization artifacts without proving they belong to the current source.
The orchestrator skips ASR on resume based only on output-file existence, with no source or content identity check.
Every resumed run re-adds ID3 frames to all prior WAVs instead of only newly created chunks.
ZIP generation never removes obsolete volumes from a previous run using the same output stem.
Missing source WAVs are skipped while the partial ZIP is still atomically installed and reported as completed.
Sanitized volume names are not guaranteed to remain unique across metadata groups.
Numeric CLI options are accepted without range or finiteness validation even though downstream code requires bounded values.
A skipped entry is stored in decisions and therefore is unconditionally skipped on every later run.
Quitting on an undecided entry advances and checkpoints the cursor past that entry's proposed source span.
Auto-keeping pre-anchor entries makes the later fresh-session divergence check think the session is resumed.
The auto-approval threshold is not constrained to a meaningful probability range.
Targeted reset bypasses the tolerant checkpoint loader and crashes on a corrupt checkpoint that normal review would recover from.
Targeted reset indexes physical JSONL lines although normal loading indexes nonblank entry records.
find_best_match keeps the earliest window when multiple windows have the same best ratio rather than preferring the candidate nearest the cursor.
Auto-anchor returns the first merely acceptable entry instead of the strongest or earliest high-confidence entry among the attempts.
Broadcasting one annotation token across several source words duplicates its leading and trailing pause markers on every word.
Alignment-quality simulation advances its cursor only at a hardcoded 0.45 even when the caller's acceptance threshold is lower.
The loader always requests all model layers on GPU and unconditionally declares a successful test inference to be GPU execution.
An empty dataset is treated as a successful annotation phase even though no output archive is created.
Malformed batch annotations are coerced with str() instead of being rejected and retried.
A syntactically valid but structurally invalid checkpoint is not repaired before the caller appends new entries.
The resume owner marker identifies only an absolute pathname, not the audio content or version at that path.
Resume safety is not keyed to chunking, filtering, enrichment, diarization, model, or metadata settings.
Phase artifacts are written directly to their final paths rather than through a temporary file and atomic replacement.
WAV durability fsyncs the file but not the dataset_temp directory entry before committing metadata.
All runs share one un-locked dataset_temp directory and identical sample/checkpoint filenames.
Compare checkpoints are keyed only by JSONL pathname and contain no source, output, or input-content identity.
The final corrected JSONL is overwritten in place without an atomic temporary file.
Phase forwarding filters raw argv tokens rather than forwarding the parsed argument namespace.
The enrichment subprocess resolves llm_enricher.py from the caller's current directory instead of the preparer script directory.
The enrichment phase hardcodes 10-second chunks instead of honoring the annotation chunk size.
The enriched output changes from llm_enricher's list shape to a word-segment dict shape without an atomic or resumable contract.
Resumed checkpoint audio_filepath values are trusted as both filesystem paths and ZIP entry names.
Untrusted EPUB and metadata text is printed directly to an interactive terminal without neutralizing control sequences.
Untrusted EPUB archives are decompressed and parsed without entry-count, uncompressed-size, or expansion limits.
A caller-supplied scratch path is trusted as generated-owned data and is unconditionally deleted after annotation.
Compare reimplements the canonical source-cleanup pipeline instead of calling `clean_source_text`.
Source loading, cleanup, tokenization, and initial-cursor selection are duplicated between compare and preparer instead of sharing `_build_source_state`.
The three-tier source-recovery sequence is copied independently in compare, the preparer, and the quality estimator rather than extracted into one alignment helper.
Per-item LLM response extraction, validation, source merge, sanitization, and success accounting are copy-pasted across per-chunk, full-batch fallback, and tail-batch paths.
The preparer duplicates the emphasis and pause normalization already implemented by the shared annotation parser.
The progress tracker silently reports an unknown dynamic step as step 1 instead of registering it.
The public --skip-annotation option is retained but always rejected as unimplemented.
Importing the preparer creates a log file immediately and adds handlers to a global logger every time the module is loaded.
Annotation startup logs a hardcoded `-1` layer policy even though the loader explicitly requests 99 layers.
The monolithic annotation loop embeds separate full-batch and tail-batch implementations instead of routing both through one flush function.
Batch-level failures are counted as one failed chunk even when every per-chunk fallback succeeds.
The supposedly streaming oversized-WAV decoder captures the entire PCM stream in memory and then allocates a second full float array.
Every non-overflowed long input is still loaded completely at native resolution before resampling.
Full diarization reads the entire audiobook into an in-memory float tensor.
Oversized audio is decoded independently to 24 kHz scratch and 16 kHz ASR arrays, doubling source decode work.
Batch progress and ETA calculations use inconsistent batch boundaries and the current chunk's start time rather than the whole batch's start time.
ASR --limit does not limit expensive diarization because diarization runs before transcription and limit handling.
Wav2Vec2 computes a full vocabulary softmax for every frame solely to derive a rough confidence value.
Compare rewrites the entire growing decisions dictionary after every manual decision.
Resume loads and test-infers the full LLM before determining whether any ASR words remain to process.
The quality pre-scan repeats the expensive alignment work for the first 30 entries immediately before the interactive loop aligns them again.
EPUB title/author extraction runs in the parent and again in every phase subprocess even though only annotation needs the derived name.
Per-book proper-noun policy is stored in mutable module-global state rather than passed as alignment context.
Run identity, checkpoints, and intermediate phase artifacts are attached to a global working directory instead of a per-source run manifest.
Speaker diarization is bolted onto duration-based chunks after the fact rather than making speaker turns a chunk boundary invariant.
The phase orchestrator is a special raw-argv rewriting layer instead of a shared parsed-command runner.
Segmented output has no managed-volume manifest or lifecycle, so correctness depends on callers manually cleaning old names.
The annotation phase infers optional inputs solely from whether stale files happen to exist instead of consuming an explicit phase manifest.
Output names are derived only from the audio stem, so distinct inputs with the same basename overwrite or masquerade as one another.
Resume validation treats any existing output path as a completed dataset without checking ZIP validity or nonzero content.
Folder discovery admits directories and other non-files merely because their names have audio extensions.
The `--source` sanity check accepts directories and other non-files because it tests only existence.
Numeric CLI options are not constrained to meaningful ranges or finite values.
Fuzzy source selection silently chooses whichever equal-scoring file `os.scandir` yields first.
The KeyboardInterrupt path kills an unresponsive child but does not reap it after SIGKILL.
The subprocess uses a preparer path relative to the caller's working directory rather than this script's directory.
This GPU-heavy batch processor launches TTS subprocesses without the project's global GPU lock.
The final batch receipt is written in place rather than atomically.
Every audio file scans the entire source directory once for the validation summary and again for processing.
A normal comma-separated NVIDIA device selector is passed as one invalid `-i` value.
The ROCm VRAM gate always inspects the first card and ignores `HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES` or `ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES`.
Queue-log write failures are ignored even though queue state is part of the wrapper's safety contract.
Failure to create a pending marker is silently ignored.
Default paths are not reliably anchored when the script is invoked through PATH by bare name.
Only INT and TERM reap the child process group, leaving SIGHUP and SIGKILL as orphaning paths.
The dirty-state hash records only the count of untracked harness files, not their identities or contents.
The user-controlled job name is interpolated directly into a filesystem path and log records.
Command provenance flattens argv into `$*`, losing argument boundaries and exact reproduction.
The dirty gate recognizes only a few untracked extensions, so an untracked executable or fixture can alter an experiment while the tree is reported clean.
The append-only queue log has no size bound or rotation.
A gate artifact may point to an adapter from any supported retrain campaign, not necessarily the selected campaign.
When the gate's adapter path is unusable, the promoter silently falls back to a same-named directory that was never tied to that gate.
Promotion checks only that the source directory exists, not that the core adapter weight and config files are present and valid.
The advertised fail-closed behavior does not handle unreadable evidence files.
Gate and baseline scores are not validated as finite real numbers.
Rollback does not remove manifest fields that promotion added when the original metadata lacked them.
Rollback deletes each live adapter before validating or staging the complete replacement.
Promotion, backup, rollback, and manifest updates have no shared file lock or transaction journal.
Live adapter files, manifest, and receipt are overwritten non-atomically without crash recovery.
Adapter names and rollback stamps are accepted without validating that they remain inside the model and backup roots.
The manifest metadata field list is duplicated in promotion and rollback.
The promotion receipt is below the provenance needed to audit exactly what was installed.
`--dry-run` is documented as an alignment pre-scan but is only a stub that writes a header and exits successfully.
Per-pair `run_with_restart.sh` failures are ignored and the script can still finish with status 0.
Aggregation scans every preparer log ever left in the shared logs directory rather than logs produced by this corpus.
The report derives each run label by blindly slicing 22 characters from a filename rather than parsing the log stem.
`--aggregate` and `--help` still require `AUDIO_DIR` and `SOURCE_DIR` even though they do not need to discover or pair inputs.
Shell paths are interpolated directly into Python source strings rather than passed as argv or environment data.
The corpus runner invokes a GPU-heavy preparer directly instead of through the shared GPU lock.
The script slices and `exec`s source text from another Python file to obtain one matcher instead of importing the matcher from a dependency-free helper module.
Corpus outputs again use only the audio basename and can collide.
Every preparer log is read wholly into memory solely to run a handful of regular expressions.
The four-row pilot validator does not require the documented adapter, seed, pair matrix, or fixed arguments.
Category run sizes are hard-coded separately from the category list and matrix construction.
Malformed artifact shapes escape as incidental `TypeError`, `KeyError`, `IndexError`, or `StopIteration` rather than `ArtifactValidationError`.
All hundreds of WAV artifacts are fully decoded serially during each validation run.
Checkpoint orchestration uses non-atomic existence checks without a run lock, allowing two invocations to generate the same artifacts concurrently.
The strict validators assume every nested checkpoint object has the expected container types.
An installed distribution is accepted from metadata without importing it, so a broken native package can be reported healthy.
A required version mismatch is recorded only as a note and still leaves the environment OK.
The fallback for an absent or empty `rocm_python` setting does not match the app's documented running-interpreter default.
The app environment specification omits runtime packages required by the app and the in-repo Voice Lab stages.
The doctor duplicates Voice Lab config resolution instead of calling the same resolver used by the app.
Running-job detection reads only the last 200 queue-log lines.
Queue-log parsing truncates a job name at its first space.
Pause status can report VRAM only on AMD and says unknown on supported NVIDIA hosts.
The status path never reports a live job's ETA despite the project requirement to report ETA whenever a GPU/LLM job is running.
Pending markers are considered live using only `kill -0 PID`, which is vulnerable to PID reuse and has no start-time token.
The shared stage helper requires Bash 4 associative arrays although the public installer supports macOS's system Bash 3.
A dependency-skipped stage is not counted as a failure, so a chain with no measured stages can pass its summary.
VRAM reclamation happens before dependency checks, so a stage guaranteed to be skipped can still stop the shared LLM server.
`--needs-vram` stops the server before acquiring the GPU lock.
Artifact commits stage the entire shared experiments directory, despite claiming to isolate the current stage.
Failure to stage or commit artifacts is converted into a successful no-op.
Exit code 124 is treated categorically as a GNU timeout even though a wrapped command may deliberately return 124 itself.
VRAM and server lifecycle policy is bolted into a generic stage helper as a pre-stage special case instead of being part of the locked job infrastructure.
The expensive LLM is loaded before the input path and JSON are validated.
The top-level transcript container and each chunk are not validated as dictionaries.
Prompt construction occurs outside the method's advertised failure boundary.
The non-code-block JSON regex cannot parse nested JSON objects.
Local full-offload LLM inference is initialized without the global LLM/GPU lock.
The output transcript is written in place without an atomic helper.
This standalone enricher reimplements model loading rather than using the app's active LLM profile and shared inference infrastructure.
A generated book is called complete solely when it has more than 50 entries, with no status or expected chunk count.
The INT and TERM trap only restores configuration and returns, so interrupted execution can continue.
The 12-hour timeout has no kill-after escalation.
The lock bypass sentinel is trusted without verifying the PID exported by the real lock holder.
The chain hardcodes one machine's repository path instead of deriving the checkout location.
ROCm JSON parsing returns after the first line beginning with `{`, even if that opener is a warning rather than the payload.
Missing public or private source texts are silently skipped during staging.
The text-fidelity stage omits one of the four generated PDNC books.
The strict stage summary is not the last command, so later echoes erase its failure status.
Any nonempty output file is treated as a completed per-book result.
The pooled scorer trusts `n` without checking that either arm contains that many complete rows.
Missing or malformed halves do not make the confirmation chain fail; it simply prints no comparison.
The chain starts or replaces the shared server before taking the GPU lock.
The second Goal 1.3 chain repeats the nonempty-file completion bug.
This is effectively a copy of the 2026-08-30 Goal 1.3 chain with only adapter and tag substitutions.
The Japanese ASR stage skips any existing output without checking completion.
Baseline identity-measurement failures are logged but never affect the final result.
The script prints the number of rank-2 gate failures but never exits nonzero for them.
Existing gate artifacts are accepted based on a grep substring rather than parsed verdict and completeness.
A missing held-out split is logged as a skip but not as incomplete work.
The preparer restart wrapper launches a GPU job directly and has no lock acquisition or inherited-lock validation.
TERM sent only to the wrapper is not forwarded or trapped, so the child can continue after the restart supervisor exits.
The `extra_args` array is initialized but never used.
When readiness times out, the newly launched server process is not killed.
The log parent is not created or validated before background redirection.
Readiness checks only that `/v1/models` responds, not that the requested model and LoRA are actually loaded.
Server inspection and replacement are not protected by a shared lock.
The script kills every process named `llama-server`, not only the server for its configured port or model.
Multiple expensive research stages use bare file existence as a completion guard.
Existing gate artifacts are again accepted based only on grep text.
A CPU-only release verification is unnecessarily wrapped in the GPU queue.
Artifact freshness uses whole-second mtimes and a one-second tolerance, allowing a pre-run artifact to be mistaken for the current recheck.
Recheck classification uses only the process exit code and does not require a fresh score artifact.
A missing or empty recheck roster is treated as zero tests and therefore a successful stage.
The chain kills the global llama-server outside any GPU lock.
The adoption probe derives an import path from `__file__` inside Python read from stdin instead of receiving the repository path.
An UNKNOWN adoption result is treated like no server, after which the script starts a second server without stopping or replacing the unknown one.
The readiness loop checks an empty PID after adopting a server, so it stops after the first failed probe.
Malformed pilot JSON is converted into a nonfatal gate failure rather than a checkpoint error.
Any existing confirmatory file is accepted as a complete experiment.
The INT and TERM cleanup handler does not terminate the campaign after cleanup.
Server adoption checks alias, context, and reasoning but not the actual model file or adapter identity.
A stale config backup is not restored before being overwritten on the next run.
Every stage wrapper deliberately returns success, so the overnight chain cannot report failed books or timeouts through its exit code.
Server readiness uses curl without HTTP failure semantics and does not stop waiting when the server process dies.
The chain starts a raw llama-server without the identity checks and concurrency protocol in `ensure_llama_server.sh`.
The unstaged gate uses `git diff`, which cannot see untracked generated files.
The derived-file regeneration script is executed twice solely to retrieve its Python path.
The four-arm separator table limits each arm to 800 although its guard requires all four arms at 1,600 terms.
Dot-arm completeness checks only a top-level status string.
The strict summary is followed by explanatory output that overwrites its failure status.
Skipping the required separator table is not recorded as a chain failure.
This older unseen-books chain overwrites a stale configuration backup before restoring it.
Book subprocess results are neither inspected nor used to determine the final status.
Its signal trap restores config but does not exit or return a signal failure.
A fresh installation never installs the app-environment `llama_cpp` build required by the current Voice Lab profiling stage.
The Whisper source clone and model download have no commit integrity or checksum verification.
The same long inline Python constraint generator is duplicated for two environments.
A nonempty result file is treated as complete without validating status or row count.
The GPU job's exit code is reported but never used to fail the chain.
Experiment provenance hardcodes an AMD 9070 XT even when the chain runs on another GPU or backend.
The chain can replace the global llama-server before acquiring any GPU lock.
Failure to build the re-gate queue is not checked and can become a successful zero-adapter run.
The final diagnostic grep makes the script fail when gate outcomes are unchanged, even though that is an explicitly valid result.
Individual identity gates have no timeout inside the long-held outer GPU job.
Existing gate artifacts are overwritten in place one at a time without a checkpoint or final completeness validation.
The runaway stop-gate is bypassed whenever it wrote any nonempty file, regardless of verdict.
Prepare, build, and training stages use nonempty-file checks rather than validated completion.
Generation has no `--requires-ok` dependency on the stop gate or earlier training stages.
The narration/quotes stop-gate is treated as satisfied by any nonempty output, including a failed verdict.
Reader 2033 repeats the nonempty stop-gate bypass.
The 4992 and 2033 LibriQuote chains are near-verbatim reader-specific copies.
The generic attempt helper skips every existing artifact, including reports and checkpoints known to be written on failure.
The queue records failure count in text but ultimately returns success.
A date-specific hardcoded deadline is evaluated even when the chain is accidentally run later.
The chain's custom server shutdown is not serialized with GPU work.
Retraining batch exit codes are printed but never checked.
The adapter list is consumed without validating existence, comments, blank lines, or IDs.
The supposedly restartable batched retraining does not pass `--resume`.
Experiment scripts repeatedly hardcode one user's repository and data paths instead of using a shared experiment context.
This chain uses a private `PAUSE_GPU_QUEUE` file in addition to the repository's `gpu_pause.sh` flag mechanism.
Lock-wrapper boilerplate is copied into many chains instead of being provided by a shared re-exec helper.
Server startup, model selection, logging, readiness, and cleanup are reimplemented instead of using `ensure_llama_server.sh` and a shared identity mechanism.
The corpus report scrapes human-readable log text rather than consuming a structured preparer manifest.
Failure of the Python program that builds the remaining-replay list is ignored and treated as an empty list.
A failed or timed-out generation is followed by scoring of whatever partial or stale output file remains.
The paired scorer appends to a report directory that this script never creates.
A score path is added to the comparison list even when its generation or scoring stage failed.
The attempt helper converts every failed stage into a successful function result.
The optional SageAttention wheels are hard-coded for CPython 3.10 while the installer does not ensure that interpreter version.
The purported second 200-term sample is actually the same deterministic first 200 terms measured again with the same default voice.
A failed later producer leaves earlier index files rewritten despite the message claiming the tree is not left half-updated.
The inline completeness check treats many partial or malformed artifacts as complete.
The chain continues into an eight-hour generation even after the required LLM server failed to start.
The script claims to switch the pipeline to Qwen3-14B but never modifies config.json or passes --model to the experiment.
A failed regression generation is converted into a zero exit status by the later diagnostic commands.
Per-book failures are printed but do not make this end-to-end validation script fail.
The Chinese alignment-diagnosis stage points at the Japanese ASR build.
A syntactically valid but non-object JSON artifact is classified as merely incomplete and overwritten.
The pilot gate accepts three measured rows but then reports that four of four rows cleared.
The resume driver treats any existing pilot output as final and therefore cannot resume an interrupted pilot.
A missing language build is skipped but the final quality stage still unconditionally consumes that language's manifest.
Identity-gate failures are logged but never affect the final status of the regate chain.
Only exit code 130 is handled, so every actual corpus failure is silently accepted.
The watchdog declares completion if the tmux session has not appeared within ten seconds.
The gate verification script only prints expected exit codes and never asserts them.
Failure of the refusal-stratification stage is discarded and omitted from the shared stage summary.
A failed index refresh is only logged and is not represented in the final stage summary.
The idempotence check accepts any healthy service on the port without verifying its model, adapter, context, or KV settings.
The Pinokio LLM launcher still requires the obsolete sibling-repository environment.
An explicitly supplied invalid PYTHON or CONFIG value is silently replaced with a hard-coded main-checkout path.
Generation and scoring failures are ignored, allowing stale artifacts to flow into the final comparison.
A failed recipe leaves the shared status file saying START rather than recording failure.
A failed nvidia-smi provenance query does not stop the evaluation and the experiment runs without EXPERIMENT_ENV.
Reset omits the active character_aliases.json file even though it removes other active-book state.
The readiness loop accepts an already-running service on port 8090 before checking whether the launched server is alive.
The script sets REPO to the archive directory rather than the repository root.
The archived ASR chain mistakes its own directory for the repository root.
The archived overnight chain likewise computes the wrong repository root.
The extended archive chain uses the archive directory as REPO and cannot reach repository tools.
The dynamically located checkout is immediately abandoned in favor of a hard-coded main checkout for the model manifest and auxiliary binaries.
The stage helper explicitly converts every GPU failure into a successful script result.
The self-reexec GPU guard trusts a caller-controlled environment sentinel and can therefore be bypassed.
The Python GPU wrapper points gpu_job.sh at the obsolete home-directory lock rather than the repository lock.
Any git-status failure is converted into a clean tree by the command substitution and trailing true.
chain_running uses substring process matching and can wait on unrelated commands that merely mention the target filename.
The identity gates load TTS and ECAPA models directly without taking the shared GPU lock.
Dependent prune, package, training, and scoring stages are not gated on the success of their predecessors.
Nonempty partial files are treated as proof that training and gating stages completed.
A VRAM-heavy llama-server is started before the chain acquires the GPU lock.
Server cleanup sends TERM but does not wait for VRAM to be released.
The chain globally kills every llama-server process rather than managing only a server it owns.
The completion guard does not verify that the artifact was produced with the currently requested clip count.
The artifact filename omits E_ROW_LIMIT, so a completed smaller run blocks every later widened run.
artifact_complete accepts status=complete without validating row counts or the requested limit.
Every nonempty fidelity output is treated as a complete seed.
The model is saved directly into the final destination with no temporary directory or completion marker.
Reset stops only start.js while independent Pinokio jobs can continue writing the files being removed.
Update mutates the checkout and virtual environment without first stopping the running app or LLM daemon.
The cloud Qwen comparison loads a multi-billion-parameter model without any GPU lock or VRAM check.
The archived chain explicitly uses the obsolete home-directory lock rather than the repository mutex.
The EXIT trap can overwrite concurrent configuration edits with an old fixed backup even though this run passes --model explicitly and does not edit config.
A server that remains alive but never becomes ready is not terminated before the script exits.
Starting a selected GGUF updates only llm.base_url and never updates llm.model_name to the selected model.
Index validation uses raw substring matching rather than checking indexed artifact records.
Stage 7 manually runs only two of the four index producers instead of the repository's canonical refresh_indexes.py.
The Chatterbox result records neither the installed source commit nor the model revision used.
The Qwen comparison pins neither the model revision nor the qwen-tts package version in its evidence.
The endpoint guard accepts any advertised model containing qwen3 rather than the required qwen3-14b.
The resume loop regenerates arms 1 through 3 but assumes arm 0 exists without validating it.
The launcher treats the first arbitrary HTTP-looking substring in process output as the app URL.
The replay command obtained from an artifact is executed through eval without validation.
A predictable /tmp pathname is opened for writing without O_EXCL or mktemp.
Unvalidated SEP and LIMIT values are interpolated into artifact and work paths that can traverse outside the runtime directory.
Optional native packages are installed from mutable Hugging Face main URLs without a revision or checksum.
The user-supplied model filename is inserted into a shell command with only hand-written double quotes and no shell escaping.
The artifact helper stages an entire shared directory and commits every already-staged change.
The comparison clones and executes the current default branch rather than a reviewed commit.
Executable and model paths supplied through overridable environment variables are expanded without quoting.
The script reimplements config mutation with json.dump instead of the existing atomic_json_write helper.
The chain duplicates process-waiting logic instead of using run_chains/lib/queue.sh's wait_for_chain helper.
The chain maintains its own stage runner instead of using the shared run_chains/lib/stage.sh implementation.
The chain hard-codes the main checkout instead of using the existing repo-relative and resolve_python conventions.
The default Python environment still points at the removed sibling-repository environment instead of this repository's app/env.
The resolver invokes regen_derived.sh three separate times instead of obtaining its interpreter and path list through the shared generation interface once.
The corrected continuation chain retains an unused start_server function and related server path setup that can no longer execute.
The score column is parsed from the voice list but never used or validated.
The same artifact-completeness algorithm is copy-pasted across numerous chains and has already diverged in related files.
The Stage 7 entry point hard-codes 75 even though the full matrix size and manifest are loaded dynamically.
Reset consists of many repeated fs.rm steps instead of a data-driven list of active project artifacts.
The menu module imports Node filesystem and path modules that it never uses.
Each CPU scoring stage is serialized between GPU generation stages, leaving the expensive card idle during scoring.
The eight-voice chain alternates expensive generation and CPU-only prosody scoring instead of batching all GPU work first.
The resume script never skips arms that are already complete and always regenerates and rescores arms 1 through 3.
The downloader instantiates the full Whisper model in memory only to serialize it.
The shared chain waiter sleeps in fixed two-minute intervals and can waste up to nearly two minutes after every completed predecessor.
One outer GPU job holds the lock for queue setup, JSON analysis, every artifact replay, and logging even when individual replay commands are not uniformly GPU workloads.
Every start overwrites the single shared server log and polls serially for up to ten minutes.
Each index subprocess captures all stdout and stderr in memory even though output only needs to be summarized.
GOALS.md's generated line-number conflict is handled with a one-off marker parser bolted onto the generic resolver.
Model-specific server flags and lifecycle logic are duplicated across several chains instead of being expressed through a managed server runner.
Pruning, dataset packaging, training, and scoring are expressed as a shell-level ad hoc dependency chain rather than declared stages with success dependencies.
Native acceleration choices are encoded as platform-specific command-line branches rather than a shared installer capability matrix.
Reset is implemented as an incomplete manual file list rather than a centrally defined active-project-state boundary.
The repository has several incompatible preflight policies, with this helper excluding selected generated files while individual chains reimplement broader or narrower dirty-tree behavior.
Single-task cancellation never sets state['cancel'] after a PID exists, disabling the promised TERM-to-KILL escalation and often recording the cancellation as a failure.
Subprocess output uses the platform default strict text decoder, so one non-UTF-8 byte can kill the reader and strand the task.
Windows cancellation escalation kills only the wrapper process instead of the descendant process tree.
Review report filenames have only one-second resolution and can overwrite an earlier report.
The supposedly finite LLM timeout accepts negative, infinite, and NaN environment values.
Malformed built-in manifest entries are not validated before mandatory id lookup.
Every run of three replacement characters is collapsed as a repetition even when it is simply three lost letters in a word.
The shared generation preflight applies repairs without running the structural-regression check enforced by the CLI.
Partial repairs are discarded whenever the number of health findings stays equal, even if some findings were genuinely repaired.
The merge command validates without source_text, so valid book-supported speakers absent from the local passage are falsely labeled invented.
Merge always records the hard-coded default run when batches came from a different custom run.
Invented-name validation checks only the first token of a multi-word answer.
CLI alias groups are neither whitespace-normalized nor transitively closed before agreement comparison.
The top-level llm_failover boolean is the one known AppConfig field omitted from stored-value validation.
API verification checks only summary self-consistency and therefore accepts an empty test suite.
Unexpected gate exceptions leave the JSON report marked running even though its individual gate says failed.
Quoted dialogue containing only one character is always excluded.
Source mapping identifies entries by only their first 120 normalized characters.
Repeated sentence adverbs can be promoted to authoritative speaker labels because the exclusion list is finite.
Review-store loading assumes any truthy JSON value is a dictionary.
Failure to consume a submitted session is swallowed, allowing the same decision to be recorded repeatedly.
Session consumption and review persistence form a non-atomic two-file transaction in which a crash loses the decision.
The six-hour session age limit is enforced only opportunistically during session creation, not when audio is served or a decision is submitted.
Pruning accepts ISO timestamps without a timezone and then compares them to an aware UTC cutoff.
Manifest loading does not catch UnicodeDecodeError, contradicting its one-bad-file isolation guarantee.
Nested manifest and telemetry shapes are trusted despite the loader validating only the top-level chunks list.
Duplicate model decisions for one item can be counted in both decisions and refusals, producing impossible run totals.
